title: £45 a Year for 9,000 Years: Arthur Guinness at St James's Gate
conflicts: Annual rent is £45 in every source checked. The £100 is the godfather's bequest that funded Leixlip (Guinness Archive, Storehouse); Come Here To Me and Wikipedia also report a £100 up-front payment to the Rainsfords, which the story does not assert. Water dispute: Archive says he 'won his point' and kept free water, while Yenne (via Wikipedia) has a 1785 settlement at £10 a year; the story says only what the archive records for 1775.
notes: Guinness Archive fact sheet and the FAQ ('lease no longer valid ... purchased the lands outright') are cited from Internet Archive copies. The 9,000-year term's motive is not documented; Roger Protz's reading (confidence) is attributed. A St James's Gate fact-sheet PDF was dropped because the Internet Archive copy loaded only intermittently.
